Forming the present subjunctive

It's the hallmark of the B1 level. The three singular persons are identical, which is why people often add the pronoun: “che io parli”, “che tu parli”.

parlareprenderedormirefinire
io, tu, luiparliprendadormafinisca
noiparliamoprendiamodormiamofiniamo
voiparliateprendiatedormiatefiniate
loroparlinoprendanodormanofiniscano

You already know these forms: they're the formal (Lei) imperatives you saw in Salerno (parli, prenda, vada, faccia).

When to use it

English has almost lost its subjunctive (it survives in “I insist that he be on time”), so this is new territory. Italian uses it after wanting, emotions and necessity, and it goes even further: it also requires it after an opinion.

TriggerExample
opinionPenso che sia tardi
doubtNon credo che venga
hopeSpero che tu stia bene
wantingVoglio che tu venga
emotionHo paura che piova
necessityBisogna che partiate
benché, prima che…Benché sia stanco, esco

So “I think he is late” is “Penso che sia in ritardo”. Same with spero che, where English says “I hope he'll come” or “I hope he comes”. Note too that English “I want you to come” becomes “I want that you come”: voglio che tu venga.

When to do without it

Certainty: indicative. “So che è vero”, “Secondo me è vero”.

Same subject in both clauses: di + infinitive. “Penso di partire” (I'm thinking of leaving), “Spero di rivederti” (I hope to see you again).
